setup.name: Espresso grinder (Mahlkonig E65W)
setup.note: Mahlkonig E65W Grind-by-Sync: $3,099.00 at Visions Espresso (sale price; list $3,199), seen November 14, 2026. The E65S at $2,099 that the first pass used is marked discontinued (2025 update) and out of stock, so a new shop cannot buy it. Lifespan is my estimate.

setup.name: Second grinder for decaf (Mahlkonig E65W)
setup.note: A second Mahlkonig E65W at $3,099.00 seen at Visions Espresso on November 14, 2026 (the E65S at $2,099 is discontinued and out of stock). A cheaper used or entry-level grinder is the usual way to save here; no listing was checked for it.

setup.name: Three-compartment sink, hand sink, mop sink and faucets
setup.note: Seen at WebstaurantStore on November 14, 2026: Regency 60-inch three-compartment sink $649.00; Regency wall-mount hand sink with gooseneck faucet $82.99-$89.99; Regency floor mop sink $234.49-$349.99 (I take $279.99). Faucets, pre-rinse and fittings stay the research notes' $500 allowance, not seen: $649 + $90 + $280 + $500 = $1,519. Plumbing labor is in the build-out. The Health Code requires a hand-washing sink near every place food is prepared and in each restroom.

setup.name: Food Service Establishment Permit
setup.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
setup.note: NYC Business, seen November 14, 2026: the permit fee for most food service establishments is $280.00 a year, plus $25.00 if you make frozen desserts (soft serve, gelato); you can open 22 days after you submit the application even if no pre-permit inspection has taken place, or call 212-676-1600 for a pre-operating inspection to open sooner. The application asks for proof of workers' compensation and disability insurance, a Food Protection Certificate or course registration, and the sales tax Certificate of Authority. The clock starts when the build-out is finished: the Health Department checks the finished room. The permit does not pass to a buyer of an operating business: the new owner applies again.

setup.name: Batch brewer, bulk grinder and airpots
setup.note: Bunn CWTF15-APS automatic brewer (item 234230010006): $980.00 at WebstaurantStore, seen November 14, 2026, matching the research notes' KaTom price. Plus the notes' $800 allowance for a bulk grinder and airpots (not seen). Drip coffee is the fastest thing on the menu at the morning peak.

setup.name: Dining Out NYC sidewalk cafe license
setup.agency: NYC Department of Transportation (Dining Out NYC)
setup.note: Dining Out NYC fees, seen November 14, 2026: $1,050 license for a four-year term + $1,500 refundable security deposit for a sidewalk cafe ($2,500 for a roadway cafe, plus a $500-$900 public hearing fee) = $2,550; on top comes a yearly revocable consent fee of $6, $10, $18 or $31 per sq ft by sector (a 120 sq ft sidewalk cafe pays $720-$3,720 a year). The 240-day wait is the Transportation Department's own eight-month timeline; the Comptroller found on October 27, 2026 that more than half of approved restaurants waited over 19 months, only 28.6% of nearly 5,000 applications from 2024 to mid-June 2026 were approved, and 1 of 388 filed in 2026. Never part of a starter kit.

roadmap.title: Get your Food Service Establishment Permit
roadmap.text: Apply online with proof of workers' compensation and disability insurance, the sales tax Certificate of Authority and the Food Protection Certificate. The fee is $280 a year. You may open on the 22nd day after applying; call for a pre-operational inspection if you want to open sooner.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)

staff.name: Barista
staff.note: NY Department of Labor OEWS file (wages updated to the first quarter of 2026), New York City region, SOC 35-3023 Fast Food and Counter Workers, the occupation that holds baristas: median $36,545.83 a year ($17.57 an hour at 2,080 hours), mean $39,310.12 ($18.90), entry $35,510.25 ($17.07). OEWS wages include tips. A shop that pays the full $17.00 minimum with no tip credit and lets baristas keep their tips pays $17-$19; $18 is my middle. The research notes planned $21, which is above the market median even before tips. The tipped rate of $11.35 + $5.65 credit is legal only with written notice and tips that cover the gap (12 NYCRR 146-1.3).

staff.name: Shift lead
staff.licenseRequired: NYC Food Protection Certificate (free online course, $24 exam)
staff.note: NY Department of Labor OEWS file (wages updated to the first quarter of 2026), New York City region, SOC 35-1012 First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers: median $50,060.70 a year ($24.07 an hour), mean $54,158.95 ($26.04). $24 is the median rounded. A shift lead with a Food Protection Certificate covers the rule that a certified supervisor is on site every open hour.

monthlyCosts.name: Paid sick leave cover
monthlyCosts.note: Up to 40 paid hours a year per worker for employers with 5-99 workers (DCWP): 40 h x $18 / 12 = $60 a month per worker when it is all used. Since February 22, 2026 every employer also owes 32 more hours of unpaid leave a year, available at once (DCWP adopted rules effective July 23, 2026, seen on rules.cityofnewyork.us), and 20 hours of paid prenatal leave a year under New York State law.

violations.name: Sidewalk tables without a Dining Out NYC license
violations.law: NYC Administrative Code §§19-160.1, 19-160.4, 19-160.5(c), 19-160.6; 34 RCNY §§5-10, 5-11 (Dining Out NYC)
violations.note: Dining Out NYC enforcement page, seen November 14, 2026: unlicensed setups get a penalty with no warning, $500 for the first offense and $1,000 for the second and later ones, and the Transportation Department may order the setup removed. Licensed cafes that break the design or operation rules first get a corrective action request with 30 days to fix it, then $200 and $500. Since 2026 roadway dining may run all year; seasonal roadway cafes run April 1 to November 29. The game charges $500 per citation.

violations.name: Spoiled food or cold food kept above 41°F
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.07(a), §81.09(a); 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, codes 04H and 02G
violations.note: Penalty schedule (24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C; rule text of 2021 on rules.cityofnewyork.us and the NYC Business restaurant page agree): "Cold TCS food not held at 41°F or below" (02G) $250, $300, $350, $400 or $600 by condition level I-V; "Food not protected from adulteration or contamination" (04H) the same $250-$600. Both are public health hazards that must be corrected immediately; 7 to 10 points, 28 at the worst level. Game formula: $300 in the first month, up to $600.

violations.name: No Food Protection Certificate holder on site
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.15(a); 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 04A
violations.note: Penalty schedule (24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, code 04A): "Food Protection Certificate not held by supervisor or manager of food operations" $400, a critical violation worth 10 points; a certificate that exists but cannot be shown costs $200 ($400 on default, code 18-11). Three sources disagree: the 2021 rule text on rules.cityofnewyork.us prints $600 for 04A, the NYC Business restaurant page (seen November 14, 2026) says $500-$1,000 and that the fine doubles after the second violation, and the consolidated schedule the first pass opened says $400. I keep $400 until the current consolidated Appendix 23-C is reread.

violations.name: Mice, rats or roaches; no pest control contract
violations.law: NYC Health Code §81.23(a), §81.23(b)(2); 24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C, codes 04K, 04L, 04M and 28-06
violations.note: Penalty schedule (24 RCNY Chapter 23, Appendix 23-C; adopted rule text on rules.cityofnewyork.us): rats, mice or live roaches (04K, 04L, 04M) $200, $200, $250, $300 or $350 by condition level I-V; the contract with a pest management professional and the service records not kept on the premises (28-06) $200, or $400 on default. Skipping pest control means both: $200-$350 + $200 = $400-$550. Game formula: $400 in the first month, up to $550. Scoring: 5 to 8 points, 28 at the worst level, which alone means a C. The NYC Business restaurant page (seen November 14, 2026) states $500-$1,000 for evidence of pests and that the fine doubles after the second violation: it disagrees with the schedule, and the schedule is the legal text. The Health Code requires a contract with a state-licensed exterminator (§81.23(b)). The 2 closure days are my estimate for an infestation that cannot be fixed during the inspection.

events.name: Wholesale coffee up 20%
events.text: Roasters pass on higher green coffee prices. Beans are about a quarter of what an order costs you to make.
events.note: Seen at FRED on November 14, 2026. Retail ground coffee (BLS APU0000717311, US city average): $9.457 per lb in June 2026, $9.249 in October 2026, a peak of $9.723 in April 2026. Green arabica (IMF PCOFFOTMUSDM, "Other Mild Arabica", cents per lb): 307.8 in June 2026, 359.2 in July 2026 (+16.7% in one month), 330.1 in September 2026; 276.8 in October 2024 and 409.5 in February 2025 (+48% in four months). Real signal for the event: the monthly arabica price up 15% or more. A 20% rise in the roaster's bean price x beans about 25% of cost of goods = +5% on cost of goods; both shares are my estimates.

events.name: Milk up 10%
events.text: Your dairy distributor raises prices. Milk goes into most of the drinks you sell.
events.note: Seen at FRED on November 14, 2026 (BLS APU0000709112, whole milk, US city average): $3.997 per gallon in November 2025, $4.317 in June 2026 (+8% in seven months), $4.101 in October 2026. The 10% rise and the dairy share of cost of goods (about 30%) are my estimates: 10% x 30% = +3%.

events.name: Sidewalk shed goes up on your block
events.text: Scaffolding covers your storefront while the building next door repairs its facade. Fewer people notice the shop.
events.note: Seen through search on November 14, 2026 (nyc.gov refuses this session): the City's 2024 study with Mastercard found that dining and drinking places with a sidewalk shed in front saw weekly transactions fall 3.5% to 9.7% in the six months after the shed went up, and card spending at businesses in buildings with sheds fell $3,900-$9,500 a month. I take the middle, -7%, for six months. Owners quoted in the press report 20-30% drops; those are anecdotes. Since Local Laws 48 and 51 of 2025 (in force January 2026) shed permits last 90 days, each renewal costs $130, and after 180 days the building owner pays graduated monthly penalties (up to $6,000 a month): sheds came down faster in 2026. The average shed stood 482 days in August 2023 (Citizens Union report).

events.name: NYC Restaurant Week
events.text: Prix-fixe menus at $30, $45 and $60 pull diners into the neighborhood. More people walk past your door.
events.note: NYC Tourism, seen November 14, 2026: Restaurant Week Winter 2027 runs January 19 to February 11 with prix-fixe menus at $30, $45 and $60; Saturdays are excluded and restaurants may join for one to four weeks. A coffee shop does not sell prix-fixe meals: the 5% lift is my estimate for more people out on the streets of a dining block. No measurement exists.

tipCredit.note: NY DOL, seen November 14, 2026: New York City food service workers $17.00 = cash wage of at least $11.35 + tip credit of no more than $5.65, the same from January 1, 2027 (the minimum wage does not rise on January 1, 2027 because an off-ramp condition was met). No tip credit on days when a tipped worker spends more than two hours or 20% of the shift on non-tipped work.

takeover.note: BizBuySell coffee shop and cafe valuation benchmarks (seen through search on November 14, 2026; the page itself is outside this session's network): median sale price $150,000, median asking price $175,000, median revenue $375,000, median owner earnings $78,780; sold businesses traded at a median 0.41 times revenue and an average 2.2 times earnings. Restaurants in the Northeast traded at the lowest cash-flow multiple in the country in Q2 2026, 2.05 (BizBuySell Insight Report). NYC listings seen in search: a Manhattan coffee shop asking $645,000 on $135,000 of cash flow, an East Village one at $150,000, a Staten Island cafe asset sale at $100,000. The game asks 40% of a year of sales the address supports, between $80,000 and $300,000. The buyer still signs a lease (new deposit), applies for a new Health Department permit (it does not transfer), restocks and hires. awareness 0.9 and refreshDays stay estimates waiting for evidence (research/prompts/80-codex-real-factors.md, part A).

eventCatalog.name: Minimum wage may rise to $17.60 on March 1, 2027
eventCatalog.text: The minimum wage stays $17.00 on January 1, 2027, but the Governor proposes $17.60 in New York City from March 1 if the Legislature agrees. Every hourly worker would cost 3.5% more.
eventCatalog.realSignal: State budget passes the off-ramp change; NY DOL publishes the March 1, 2027 rate
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Increases every January 2024-2026; none on January 1, 2027 because an off-ramp was met
eventCatalog.note: Seen November 14, 2026: proposal, not law. Announce it as possible in January; apply only if the real budget passes.

eventCatalog.name: Shed rules tighten: 90-day permits
eventCatalog.text: Since January 2026 a sidewalk shed permit lasts 90 days and owners pay monthly penalties after 180 days. A shed over your door now comes down sooner.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Local Laws 48 and 51 of 2025 in force January 2026; DOB penalties after 180 days (August 2026)
eventCatalog.note: Seen through search (nyc.gov refuses this session). A report to 311 about an expired shed is the player's move; the report id is a proposal for the lead.

eventCatalog.name: Workers' comp costs fall about a fifth
eventCatalog.text: New York cut workers' compensation loss costs 21.9% from October 1, 2026. Policies renewing after that date get cheaper.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYCIRB loss cost filing approved by DFS, effective October 1, 2026
eventCatalog.note: Seen through search. The overall level, not the restaurant class; insurers apply their own multipliers. Makes skipping coverage even less worth it.

mechanics.title: Payroll taxes with per-worker caps
mechanics.playerDecision: How many people to hire and at what wage (more part-timers cost more unemployment tax per dollar of wages)
mechanics.engineMath: NY UI = 4.1% of each worker's first $17,600 a year; FUTA = 0.6% of the first $7,000; disability = $17.68 per worker a year with a $60 minimum per employer. Accrue per worker from the start of the calendar year instead of one flat rate on payroll.

mechanics.title: Not every cafe sale is taxable
mechanics.playerDecision: What to sell to go: whole pastries and bags of beans in grocery form are exempt; hot drinks, anything heated, sandwiches and anything eaten in the shop are taxed
mechanics.engineMath: taxableShare = 1 - share of sales that are unheated, to go and in grocery form. For a coffee shop about 0.95-1.0; keep 1.0 until menu data exists.

mechanics.title: Where the LLC publishes its notice
mechanics.playerDecision: The LLC publishes in the county of the office named in its articles. A Brooklyn package is $1,475; Manhattan $1,795; Albany $395.
mechanics.engineMath: setup[llc_and_publication].cost = $200 + package price of the chosen county. Only a real office address in that county is lawful; the game should not offer a fake address.

unit.name: order
unit.note: Planning assumption from research notes (economics.md, 2026 planning model): an average ticket of $8.50 before sales tax (a drink, sometimes with a pastry). Menu anchors seen by the note's author in 2026: latte $4.25-$6.99, croissant $4.00-$5.49. Ingredients, food and spoilage are 26% of sales = $2.21 per order; cups, lids and napkins (another 2%) are a separate monthly cost line, so the full cost of goods is 28%. No public statistic of the average NYC cafe ticket exists (searched November 14, 2026). Input prices behind the cost line were checked: retail ground coffee $9.25 per lb and whole milk $4.10 per gallon in October 2026 (BLS via FRED), a 12 oz hot cup 4.6 cents (WebstaurantStore, $45.99 per 1,000).

options.label: Staff clean every day, deep clean once a month
options.note: My estimate: staff clean during paid shifts; $130 is chemicals, paper and one monthly deep clean. No NYC tariff exists.

options.label: Professional cleaning crew every night
options.note: My estimate: a crew a few nights a week on top of staff cleaning, $400 more than standard. Seen through search: vendor prices for small NYC commercial spaces start at $150-$500 a month for an office up to 1,000 sq ft, and restaurant cleaning runs $50-$150 an hour for a professional crew; nightly restaurant service would cost more than this option. Not a quote.

options.label: Wipe and go
options.note: My estimate: $30 of supplies. Leads to dirty_surfaces: $200-$300 and 5-8 points per citation (Appendix 23-C, code 06D).

options.label: House blend from a wholesale roaster
Specialty roaster and local dairy
options.note: My arithmetic: about 108 kg (238 lb) of beans a month for 6,000 orders at 18 g, times about $3 more per lb for a specialty roaster = $714, rounded to $750 with local dairy. The $3 premium is my estimate; retail ground coffee averaged $9.25 per lb in October 2026 (BLS via FRED).

options.label: 6am - 9pm
options.note: My arithmetic with the D12 barista wage: three more open hours a day x 30 days = 90 paid hours x $18 x 1.116 employer taxes = $1,808, plus about $200 of power and supplies = about $2,000 (the first pass had $2,300 at $21). The +8% demand is a game estimate.

options.label: Licensed exterminator, monthly visits
options.note: Seen through search (vendor pages, not quotes): monthly contracts for small NYC restaurants run about $150-$300. $175 sits in that band. The Health Code requires a contract with a state-licensed exterminator and its records on site (§81.23(b)).

options.label: Skip it
options.note: Leads to pest_activity: $200-$350 for the evidence plus $200 for no contract on site (Appendix 23-C, codes 04K-04M and 28-06).

options.label: $2 an hour above market
options.note: My arithmetic: $2 x 160 h x 4 baristas = $1,280 x 1.116 employer taxes = $1,428, rounded to $1,430. The quality and capacity effects are game estimates.

shortcuts.name: Run shifts with no certified supervisor
shortcuts.what: A Food Protection Certificate holder must be on site every hour you are open. Covering every shift means training more people and paying leads; skipping it saves about $120 a month. Each inspection that finds nobody certified costs $400 and 10 points.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: certifying and paying a lead on every shift costs about $120 a month more (the exam is $24 a person; a lead earns about $6 an hour more than a barista: NY DOL OEWS Q1 2026, NYC supervisors median $24.07 vs counter workers $17.57). The fine is $400 and 10 points (Appendix 23-C, 04A).

shortcuts.name: Sell yesterday's milk and pastries
shortcuts.what: Nothing gets thrown out: old pastries go back in the case, milk sits on the counter. Saves about 1% of sales in waste. Spoiled or warm food is a public health hazard: $250-$600 per citation and a fast road to a C grade.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: about 1% of sales is food thrown out at the end of the day. The fine for cold food above 41°F or food not protected is $250-$600 (Appendix 23-C, 02G and 04H).

shortcuts.name: Sell pastries baked at home
shortcuts.what: Baking at home instead of buying from a licensed bakery cuts pastry cost by more than half, about 3% of sales. Food from a home kitchen is food from an unapproved source: $400-$600 and a public health hazard on your record.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: pastry is about 6% of sales and home baking halves its cost = about 3% of sales. Home-cooked food is "food from an unapproved source": $400-$600 (Appendix 23-C, 03A).

shortcuts.name: Keep part of the tips
shortcuts.what: The owner takes a cut of the tip jar and the card tips: about $150 per barista a month. Tips belong to the staff by law. A wage claim returns every dollar double and reaches back six years.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: about $150 a month per barista out of tips. Labor Law §196-d forbids any part of the gratuities to the employer; §198(1-a) adds 100% liquidated damages (texts seen at nysenate.gov).

shortcuts.name: Unpaid trial shifts and training
shortcuts.what: New hires work a few shifts "on trial" and train for free: about $85 per worker a month. Every hour worked must be paid at $17.00 or more; unpaid hours are owed back double.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: about 5 unpaid hours per worker a month x $17.00 NYC minimum = $85 (NY DOL, minimum unchanged on January 1, 2027).

shortcuts.name: Long days without the extra hour
shortcuts.what: Open-to-close and split shifts stretch a workday past 10 hours. The law adds one extra hour of pay at $17.00 for each such day; skipping it saves about $135 per worker a month and is owed back double.
shortcuts.note: My arithmetic: about 8 days a month with a workday spread over 10 hours x one extra hour at $17.00 = $136 per worker (12 NYCRR §146-1.6; the minimum seen at NY DOL).

shortcuts.name: Put tables on the sidewalk without a license
shortcuts.what: A few tables outside bring about 2% more sales, and you skip the $1,050 license, the $1,500 deposit and a wait that often runs past a year. The city fines $500, then $1,000 each time, and can order the tables removed.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: a few tables outside add about 2% of sales. Unlicensed outdoor dining is fined $500, then $1,000, with no warning (Dining Out NYC enforcement page, seen).

shortcuts.name: Skip grease interceptor cleaning
shortcuts.what: Milk fat and coffee grounds fill the grease interceptor under the sink. Skipping the pump-out saves about $75 a month. Inspectors measure it: more than 25% full means a fine of $100 to $1,500, and a backup floods your floor.
shortcuts.note: My estimate: about one pump-out a quarter at $200-$330 (vendor and consumer cost guides seen through search; a Manhattan average of $329-$473 per service) = about $75 a month. Fine $100-$1,500 (NYC Business restaurant page, DEP).
